question_or_symptom: Why did an exact, descriptor-valid gfx950 SiluAndMul image execute to completion but fail its BF16 differential oracle?
observation: Decoder and route admission proved the instruction encodings and image identity, but not their numerical effects. Gem5 stores BF16 values left-aligned in a 32-bit mxfp container; packing the raw storage without shifting lost one half and misplaced the other. Packed F32 inline constants also require broadcast of the exact 32-bit float bits, and V_DIV_FMAS_F32 previously used F64 operands without committing its destination. These defects survived code-object and decode tests but were exposed by the first end-to-end BF16 oracle.
conclusion: Exact image identity, metadata, decoding, PC coverage, and complete memory coverage are necessary but insufficient operator evidence. Numerical acceptance requires executable instruction semantics and an application-visible differential oracle over the real dtype and layout.
decision: Keep exact image/descriptor/PC admission, add pure execute-semantic tests for packed modifiers, clamp ordering, divide FMA, and FP16/BF16 packing, reject finite inputs whose rounded oracle is nonfinite, and require fresh plus repeat normal-Python results with zero mismatch, nonfinite values, and fallback. Do not generalize the bounded canonical-kernel result into complete VOP conformance.
invalidated_assumptions: A decoder test plus exact code-object admission proves the arithmetic semantics needed by the kernel.
The low 16 bits of the mxbfloat16 data member contain the BF16 payload.
Correct load/store coverage means the returned BF16 values are numerically correct.
A finite BF16 input set necessarily produces a finite BF16 SiluAndMul oracle.
